content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.3) — model is overly conservative, often missing downward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, model fails to adjust downward quickly; delay in price correction by 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term trend reversion toward historical mean.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile, then converge too late.
- Overshoot after sentiment reversal: if sentiment turns from negative to positive, model often overcorrects upward, peaking too early.
- Ignore sentiment when price is near support/resistance — model ignores macro signals and defaults to historical patterns.
